source_text:
οτε λοιπὸν ἐπαύσατο μὲν ἡ καλάμη τοῦ νόμου, ωσπερ δὲ σκύβαλον
ἐχωρίσθη περιτομή, σαββάτων τήρησις καὶ τῶν αλλων, καὶ καθαρὸς ὁ τῆς πίστεως

σῖτος ὁ ἐναποκεκρυμμένος τῇ προφητικῇ καλάμῃ ἀπετέθη ταῖς ἀποθήκαις τοῦ
κοινοῦ δεσπότου. τοῦτο ουν τὸ τοῦ σκυβάλου ονομα δείκνυσιν οἰκεῖον τὸν νόμον·
καὶ ωσπερ ανευ τοῦ σκυβάλου οὐχ οιόν τε ην γενέσθαι σπόρον, ουτως οὐδὲ ανευ τοῦ
νόμου τὸ τέλειον τῆς χάριτος κατορθωθῆναι. Phil 3,13 Τὰ μὲν ὀπίσω
ἐπιλανθανόμενος, οὐχ ὡς κακά, ἀλλ' ο λέγει τοιοῦτόν ἐστιν· οὐκ ἀσχολοῦμαι εἰς τὸ
ἀναμιμνήσκεσθαι τοὺς ἀγῶνάς μου τοὺς παρελθόντας, ἀλλ' εἰς τὸ μεριμνᾶν, τί
κατορθώσω εἰς τὰ ἑξῆς. Phil 4,2 Τινὲς δὲ Εὐοδίαν ειναί φασι τὴν γυναῖκα τοῦ
δεσμοφύλακος, Συντύχην δὲ τὸν ανδρα.
thought_title: The law as refuse and the forward-looking mind
orientation: Oecumenius is closing his comments on Philippians, explaining how the law's temporary elements were set aside and how Paul's forgetting what lies behind means not dwelling on past struggles.
pass_a_gloss: So then the stalk of the law ceased, and just as refuse, circumcision, observance of sabbaths and of the other things were separated, and the pure wheat of faith, hidden in the prophetic stalk, was stored away in the barns of the common master. Therefore this name of refuse shows the law to be fitting; and just as without the refuse it was not possible for seed to come to be, so neither without the law was it possible for the perfection of grace to be accomplished. Phil 3:13 Forgetting the things behind, not as bad things, but what he says is this: I do not occupy myself with remembering my past struggles, but with being anxious about what I shall accomplish in the things ahead. Phil 4:2 But some say that Euodia is the wife of the jailer, and Syntyche the man.

choices.why: Glossary term; the stalk's separated parts are called refuse, not dung or rubbish.
Glossary term for the law and prophets as the stalk from Abraham's seed.
Glossary term for the pure grain of faith.
Glossary term for the storehouses of the common master.
Keeps the abstract noun phrase literal; 'perfection' renders τέλειον as the completed state.
Marks the reported opinion voice from the brief, not Oecumenius's own view.

pass_b_english: So then the stalk of the law ceased, and circumcision, Sabbath-keeping, and the other things were separated off like refuse, while the pure wheat of faith that had been hidden in the prophetic stalk was stored away in the barns of the common master. This very name 'refuse' shows that the law is akin to it, and just as the seed could not have come into being without the refuse, so neither could the perfection of grace have been accomplished without the law.

Philippians 3:13: 'Forgetting what lies behind'—not as though those things were evil, but what Paul means is this: I do not occupy myself with remembering my past struggles, but with being anxious about what I will accomplish in what lies ahead.
Philippians 4:2: But some say that Euodia was the wife of the jailer, and Syntyche was the man.

problems.quote: This very name 'refuse' shows that the law is fitting
problems.source_quote: τοῦτο ουν τὸ τοῦ σκυβάλου ονομα δείκνυσιν οἰκεῖον τὸν νόμον
problems.why: οἰκεῖον means 'belonging/related to,' not 'fitting'; the law is shown to be related/akin to refuse, not that it is 'fitting'
problems.fix: This very name 'refuse' shows that the law is akin to it
problems.ruling: οἰκεῖον means 'related/belonging to'; text says the name 'refuse' shows the law is akin to refuse, not that the law is 'fitting'

edits.old: This very name 'refuse' shows that the law is fitting
edits.new: This very name 'refuse' shows that the law is akin to it

last_rejected.why: Glossary requires 'steadfastness' etc. but here μεριμνᾶν means 'care/concern', not anxiety; however 'anxious' contradicts glossary spirit of 'steadfastness' as virtue. Actually: 'anxious' is wrong tone for Paul's positive care—'concern' or 'care' needed.
last_rejected.fix: but with caring about what I will accomplish in what lies ahead.
last_rejected.ruling: μεριμνᾶν ranges from 'be anxious' to 'care/concern'; 'anxious' is within normal meaning, not a major error.

last_rejected.quote: what Paul means is this: I do not occupy myself
last_rejected.source_quote: οὐχ ὡς κακά, ἀλλ' ὁ λέγει τοιοῦτόν ἐστιν· οὐκ ἀσχολοῦμαι
last_rejected.why: English hides that 'I do not occupy myself' is Oecumenius speaking in Paul's voice (first-person paraphrase), not Paul quoting himself. The voice shift is unclear.
last_rejected.fix: what he means is this: 'I do not occupy myself with remembering my past struggles, but with caring about what I will accomplish in what lies ahead.'
last_rejected.ruling: ὁ λέγει τοιοῦτόν ἐστιν· οὐκ ἀσχολοῦμαι is a first-person paraphrase; English 'what Paul means is this: I' adequately signals the voice shift.

last_rejected.quote: the seed could not have come into being without the refuse
last_rejected.source_quote: ἄνευ τοῦ σκυβάλου οὐχ οἷόν τε ἦν γενέσθαι σπόρον
last_rejected.why: Sense reversed: seed comes first, refuse follows. The Greek says seed could not come to be without refuse (i.e., refuse needed for seed's growth), but English 'come into being' suggests refuse precedes seed temporally in creation, which is awkward. Actually: 'the seed could not have been produced/grown without the refuse'—the seed needs the stalk's refuse to develop.
last_rejected.fix: just as the seed could not have grown to fruition without the refuse
last_rejected.ruling: γενέσθαι σπόρον naturally means 'come into being/be produced'; English conveys the same causal dependence without reversing sense.

last_rejected.quote: But some say that Euodia was the wife of the jailer, and Syntyche was the man
last_rejected.source_quote: Τινὲς δὲ Εὐοδίαν εἶναί φασι τὴν γυναῖκα τοῦ δεσμοφύλακος, Συντύχην δὲ τὸν ἄνδρα
last_rejected.why: English omits 'φασι' marking this as reported opinion of 'some interpreters'; 'But some say' is present but the voice marker 'some say' is only at start, not repeated for Syntyche clause, making second clause sound like authorial statement. Also 'the man' is ambiguous—should be 'her husband' or 'the husband' to match 'wife'.
last_rejected.fix: But some say that Euodia was the wife of the jailer, and that Syntyche was the husband.
last_rejected.ruling: φασι governs both clauses per Greek syntax; 'the man' for τὸν ἄνδρα is acceptable, parallel to 'wife' for γυναῖκα.
